chunks: From him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Zurarah ibn A'yan, who said:
I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) regarding the saying of Allah, the Exalted: 'The chaste women from those who were given the Book before you.'
He said: It is abrogated by His saying: 'Do not hold to the ties of marriage of the disbelieving women.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on marriage with women of the Book according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Zurarah asks Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) about the Quranic verse permitting marriage with chaste women of the People of the Book. The Imam explains that this ruling is abrogated by the verse commanding believers not to maintain marriage with polytheist/disbelieving women, indicating a shift in the legal status of such marriages. This narration is significant in Shia jurisprudence for supporting the view that the permission for marrying Jewish and Christian women was specific to the early Meccan or Medinan period and was later abrogated (naskh) by the general prohibition in Surah Al-Baqarah, aligning with the majority opinion of the Imams.
